text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Mubarak speaking in Tunis says Egypt is concerned with the peace process and cannot keep quiet about provocatory comments and lack of respect for treaties. Threats are not necessary as they lead to negative action and if (Israeli Prime Minister) Netanyahu's government wants war then that is another issue.
- Mubarak sends letters to the leaders of the UAE, Kuwait, Jordan and Lebanon on the peace process.
- At the OSCEmeeting in Lisbon: Netanyahu tries to justify settlements and calls on Egypt to reaffirm its commitment to peace!
- Egypt to increase the amount of sugar available in markets during the month of Ramadan (January and February) to 50,000 tonnes from the 25,000 tonnes available every other month.
- Egypt to sell 30 percent of fertiliser companies through the stock exchange. Cairo bourse turnover is 9.3 billion pound for the past 11 months.
- Egyptian nun says Virgin Mary told her an earthquake will strike Egypt and Israel today, spreads panic in Cairo.
- Britain's Queen Elizabeth to meet Suzanne Mubarak.
- Foreign minister Moussa tells the OSCE meeting that the peace process is in a critical phase due to Israel's practices.

- Ministerial committee says will increase the number of shares the state will offer during privatisations. The state will also offer shares in all companies it agreed to set up during the Middle East and North Africa Economic Conference.
- Egypt hangs two men for killing and mutilating a pick-up truck driver and stealing his money six years ago.
